blogTitle: Section Leader's Log (8 counts of reading per entry)
about: Hi!! I'm Becca. First chair clarinet and section leader of the 11 clarinets in the Marching Eagles, which means I know every one of their reed strengths, allergies and crushes (the crushes are confidential, the reeds are #3). Marching band is 80% walking and 20% remembering where to walk, it is absolutely a sport, and the band plays at EVERY football game but nobody has ever asked the football team to come to a concert. I count everything in 8s. It's a condition. Stand next to me for a minute and you'll hear it: 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8. Please do not say the line about band camp. I've heard it. We've all heard it. I'll tell you a real band camp story instead and it will be better.
aboutMore: Current situations: (1) the sprinklers on the practice field come on at 3:45 every day and I have never met the person who sets them. (2) Coach Dunleavy moved a home game onto the same Saturday as our regional contest and called it 'only a few hours.' It is a whole day and a bus. (3) four of my freshmen still can't find their dots. Also: I play pit clarinet for the fall musical, I'm saving for a Buffet R13 ($1,500, I have $412 and a yard sale table), and I keep a spare reed in my sock for emergencies. It has been used twice. Both times not mine.
meet: Who I'd like to meet: whoever sets the sprinklers. Coach Dunleavy, calmly, with a printed calendar and a snack. The person who invented the glide step (I have questions, mostly about knees). A tuba player who stays in step for an entire show. And all of you, in the stands, staying for halftime. Not at halftime. FOR halftime. There's a difference.

interests.General: marching band, sectionals, my clarinet (Buffet B12, student model, her name is Clara), reeds (Vandoren #3, I own 31, 6 work), the band room couch, my fanny pack (cork grease, bandaids, mints, spare reeds for all 11 clarinets and the 3 bass clarinets, who report to me spiritually. 14 in a row. Skip says it sounds like a field of geese. he's right. it's a very organized field), drill charts, counting in 8s, highlighters, being early (call time is 6:15, I arrive 5:50), the yard sale table (R13 fund)
interests.Music: the White Stripes (Seven Nation Army is a band song and we are not giving it back), Hey Ya and Hey Jude (this year's halftime show, send help), Sing Sing Sing, Benny Goodman (clarinet GOAT), Pirates of the Caribbean (every band has to play it, it's the law), Weird Al, whatever Skip's ska band is doing (the horn line is legit), the sound of 80 people stepping off together on the same count
interests.Movies: Drumline (we watch it every camp, the bus ride home is all of us quoting it), Mr. Holland's Opus, School of Rock, Rudy (don't ask, I cry), Bring It On (fine. Ashley), Hoosiers, any movie where the band gets one scene and I rewind it
interests.Television: the Rose Parade on New Year's (the bands ARE the parade, the floats are just resting), Bands of America finals on the public channel, the Macy's parade (for the bands), The Office, Friday Night Lights (brand new!! it's about football and I'm furious and I watch every week)
interests.Books: Rubank Elementary Method for clarinet, the Marching Band Drill Handbook, The Hobbit (the whole bus reads it out loud on the way to contests, one chapter per hour), the judges' score sheets (I read their comments like love letters), the band handbook (rule 14: no gum on the field)
interests.Heroes: my grandpa Ed (played clarinet in a Navy band and gave me his reed case), Mr. Pruitt (band director, says 'again' with love), Dani Rosenthal (the senior who gave me 8 counts, see blog), Benny Goodman, whoever invented the pit

keywords.band: Marching Eagles, 80 members, 11 clarinets (I'm in charge of the clarinets). We play every home game and also contests and also the pep rally and also the parade. Please don't call it 'just walking.' It's 212 counted steps in 14 minutes.
keywords.football: I respect the football team. I do. They've got a hard job. My problem is the schedule, which changes every time someone sneezes, and the band has a bus. Buses don't change.
keywords.clarinet: Buffet B12, student model, I call her Clara. 17 keys, 6 holes, one reed that works. I'm saving for an R13 ($1,500). I have $412 and a yard sale table.
keywords.camp: Two weeks in August on the blacktop at 91 degrees. Best two weeks of the year. I have 11 stories and the sousaphone one is the best. It's on my blog. If you say the line, I will hand you a clarinet and you will not be allowed to put it down.
keywords.halftime: Fourteen minutes. Eight sets. 212 counted steps. If you leave to get nachos I will see you go. I have a very good view from the 35.
keywords.drumline: Don't talk to me about drumline unless you're Bryan, in which case: yes. Come on. We have a free snare.

thad: Thad. From the pit I see the entire show from the knees down. I want you to know the Mayor has the best shoes in River City and your walk is exactly in 4/4. I counted. You're on the beat. I say that as a professional.
Thad, you asked if the pit can 'play softer when you're emoting.' We can't. A clarinet has one volume and it's 'present.' But I asked the tuba. The tuba said 'what.' That's a no.
ashley: Ashley, per the sideline schedule: cheer 6:40 to 6:55, band 6:55 to 7:10. The tubas are lined up behind the fence. If your pyramid runs over by 4 minutes, 80 people will be standing very quietly holding instruments and it is scarier than it sounds. [GREEN] (I borrowed your color. Don't tell the clarinets.)

Ashley, I watched your squad do the 3-high yesterday. That was a perfect 8-count lift. You've never dropped anyone. That's section leader energy. We should switch for a day. Not really. I'd drop a clarinet.
tyler: Tyler, your profile song is called Ants Marching and I need you to know it is NOT a marching band song. We played it once. It is 11 minutes of 7/8 and the clarinets never found the ending.

Tyler, I pet Moose in the parking lot yesterday. He stayed for the whole first half of sectionals with the truck window down. He likes the low notes. He keeps time with his tail. He's better at it than half my trumpets.
yvette: Yvette, band picture is Thursday 3:15. The sprinklers come on at 3:45. I need 80 people in uniform, in formation, DRY. I'm not asking you to move the picture. I'm asking you to find out who sets the sprinklers.

Yvette, the proof says 'Marching Eagle's.' That is a possessive of ONE eagle. There are 80 of us. [Section Leader Note. Not mad. 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8.] Thank you for putting the clarinets in the front row though.
chad: Chad!! Thank you for the sign. I think we both know it was upside down. The clarinets turned their heads sideways to read it and honestly the show got better. 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 (that's how long we looked).

Chad, you cheer for every single thing and you have never left a halftime. That's an audience member. I'm adding you to the Band Friends list. There are 3 names on it. A tuba dad. A custodian. And you.
bryan: Bryan, I'm not giving up on drumline. Snare #4 just graduated. You're not a freshman but you'd be great. I'll write your part in 4/4. Practice isn't at 6, it's at 3:45 on the dot. You don't have to answer. But you will.
Bryan, I watched you play in Greg's garage from the sidewalk. You count in your head. I saw your lips. You were counting in 8s. You're one of us. Nobody has to know.
henderson: Mr. Henderson, thank you for the science of my clarinet. I've played for six years and I had no idea about the odd harmonics. I'm going to tell everyone I'm a little odd, scientifically.
Mr. Henderson, the 6th period 'Hey Ya' is for the halftime show. I'm sorry about the 41 times. Your window faces the field, we know. We wave. Sometimes it's a salute. It's always a salute.
skip: Skip, the incident report is filed. 3 pages. I included a diagram of your route through the trombone line. It's very clean. I'm told that's not a compliment. It is also a compliment. Sectionals are Tuesday. Bring your feet.

Skip, your Pork Pie Patrol has no clarinet. Hear me out: it should. I say this as someone who hears the 'ska is not dead' speech once a week. It's not dead. But it has room for a clarinet. (A Benny Goodman one.)
tim: Tim, six copies of BLOCKFALL at the bulk rate is $10.50. I will pay in quarters, in sets of 8. I have already told the clarinets what a bulk rate is. They asked if it applies to sectionals. Also, thank you for holding the bus door with your foot. I have decided to treat that as an act of service.

Tim, your high score on SNAKE+ is 212. I know because the clarinets read it out loud on the late bus. It's now our official cadence. 2-1-2. We say it in unison. I'd like to invoice you for the lessons but I don't have a ledger. I have a binder. It has tabs.

bulletins.subject: HOW TO BE A GOOD HALFTIME AUDIENCE (an 8-step guide)
bulletins.body: 1) Stay. 2) Sit down before the show starts, not during. 3) Clap at the end of each tune, and during the clarinet solo, which is four bars. 4) Do not yell 'play something we know.' We are playing something you know. You're just not listening. 5) If you hold up a sign, check which way it faces. 6) Nachos can wait 14 minutes. 7) When the band exits the field, that's not 'the end.' That's us marching to the next thing. 8) Tell someone in the band 'that was good.' That's it. That's the whole guide. We hear it and we remember it. Counted. 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8.

dms: Quick poll, {you}. When someone says 'we just walk around at halftime,' is that (a) rude (b) wrong or (c) a 14 minute show with 212 counted steps. I'm asking about c. Thanks.
A freshman named Noelle asked me today if she's allowed to be nervous before the first game. I said that's the whole job. I don't think I've ever been so right about anything. Anyway how's your week.

A boy I don't know said the band camp line at me in the hallway today. That's number 214. I keep a tally on the inside of my band folder. He got a fact about cork grease instead. He left. I think he learned something.

Do you think the football team knows there's a score sheet for band? With judges? And a trophy? We have a trophy. It's in the case next to the football one. Ours is shinier. (It's the same size.) (Ours is shinier.)
I biked two miles to the music store for cork grease and then found it in my fanny pack. It was in there the whole time. I don't want to talk about it.
The drum major looked right at me during the run-through today. I think. He might have been looking at the press box behind me. So, basically.
Mr. Pruitt said 'good' after the Friday show. Just 'good.' Four letters. I've replayed it 31 times. I'm considering having it framed. Do you know where you get 'good' framed.

blog.title: The Football Schedule vs. Me: a timeline
blog.body: AUG 21: schedule posted. 'Final.' AUG 28: home opener moved from 7:00 to 7:30 'for the TV guy.' Which TV guy. There is no TV. SEP 11: lightning delay, 90 minutes. We stood in the end zone with our instruments in our laps and section-parent garbage bags over our shoulders. SEP 25: game moved to Saturday afternoon 'for field conditions' (the sprinklers). OCT 1: Coach Dunleavy adds a 3:30 scrimmage on the practice field. The practice field is the band's. The band has a call time. So I did the only thing I could. I stood in the end zone and counted. I am not mad at the football team. They're very good and they have a hard job. I'm mad at the calendar. It's a rectangle. And we are a block of 80 people trying to cross it in 16 counts.

blog.title: The Great Sousaphone Float: a band camp story (true)
blog.body: Band camp is two weeks in August on the blacktop behind the school at 91 degrees, and on the last Friday Mr. Pruitt takes everyone to the lake at the state park for a picnic. I'd like to say nobody planned anything. Marcy (tuba, sophomore, brave) looked at her fiberglass sousaphone, then at the lake, then at Mr. Pruitt, who was busy with the hot dogs. A fiberglass sousaphone floats. We know this now. It floated for about 11 seconds with Marcy sitting inside the bell like a canoe with a sunburn while the entire low brass stood on the dock chanting her name in perfect 4/4. When she came back, Mr. Pruitt didn't say anything for a full 8 counts and then said, 'Is it insured.' It was. There is a picture. Yvette is not allowed to put it in the yearbook. Yvette says 'we'll see.'

blog.title: why I count in 8s (a real post. no jokes. ok one joke)
blog.body: My first halftime show was freshman year, a Friday in October, and I was standing on the 35 yard line with my hands shaking so hard my clarinet was rattling. Dani Rosenthal, the senior who led the clarinets, leaned over and said, 'Becca. I only need 8 counts from you. Not the whole show. Just 8.' I got through 8. Then she said, 'ok, 8 more.' I did the entire show in sets of 8. I wasn't scared on the last chord, I was just done. Dani graduated. I have her old fanny pack. This year there's a freshman named Noelle who held her clarinet against her chest for the entire week before the first game, and I told her the same thing. Just 8 counts. She got through it. I'm still counting. The joke: I counted through my last dentist appointment and he said it went great. 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8.
